newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices remain firm.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices remain firm.

text.p: Australian wool prices remained surprisingly firm this week at sales Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said its weekly report.
The eastern market indicator rose 12 cents to 568 cents a kg clean, while the western market indicator rose 10 cents to 542 cents a kg clean since the close of sale on November 28.
A total of 132,722 bales were offered, with a pass-in rate of 9.1 percent. The number of bales offered was 92 percent of the rostered quantity advised on December 4.
"The market began the week on a firm note and this was sustained," the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.

Good quantities of all wool types were offered with both buyers and sellers being able to participate positively, the council said. "A solid level of order enquiry as also reported during the week," the council said.

Wesfarmers said the market closed on a strong note for the recess, which was primarily the result of a buyer squeeze to fill orders for shipment, as well as pressure to cover previously sold commitments.

"The relative weakness of the Australian dollar, which bottomed this week at US$0.7884, also assisted activity. This strength is expected to be sustained when sales re-open, mainly due to less wool available for sale," Wesfarmers said.
In the futures market, a total of 85 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended December 12.
Open interest decreased by 16 contracts to close at 876.
Sales resume after the Christmas recess in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle, with 88,730 bales rosterd for sale in the week commencing January 6.
